instruction: Find earnings/contextual-ASR datasets useful for natural history-dependent meeting-assistant questions and possible document tools.
scope: Focused dataset selection and a two-call text/document pilot
sub_questions: Which timestamps and speaker identities are annotated versus inferred?
Are matching documents available before a question?
Which resources help evaluate technical words, retrieval and numeric reasoning?

papers.title: Earnings-21: A Practical Benchmark for ASR in the Wild
papers.problem: Entity-dense business speech is poorly represented in common ASR tests.
papers.method: Earnings-call audio, transcripts and entity annotations.
papers.results: 39 hours across nine financial sectors; entity recognition is a central challenge.
papers.relevance: Long real multi-speaker source conversations; not already an assistant QA benchmark.
papers.limit: Transcript/text CC BY-SA terms do not establish blanket rights for all audio and third-party PDFs.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: Earnings-22: A Practical Benchmark for Accents in the Wild
papers.authors: Miguel Del Rio, Peter Ha, Quinten McNamara, Corey Miller, Shipra Chandra
papers.problem: Accented real English remains difficult for ASR.
papers.method: Global-company earnings-call corpus and transcription benchmark.
papers.relevance: More accent diversity and long discussions for a later audio pilot.
papers.limit: Manual transcripts are not a guarantee of manual word alignment; document/timing coverage must be checked per call.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: ConEC: Earnings Call Dataset with Real-world Contexts for Benchmarking Contextual Speech Recognition
papers.problem: Contextual ASR often uses artificial bias lists containing the answer.
papers.method: Adds authentic slides, releases and participant context to Earnings-21/22; corrects transcripts.
papers.results: Realistic noisy contexts support contextual ASR evaluation; pilot files include complete matching PDFs for Danaher and Monro.
papers.relevance: Best immediate match to a call-history plus document-search assistant.
papers.limit: Repository says added timestamps are automatically aligned and may be missing. Full-call participant lists are not causally safe without availability evidence; no top-level repository license was found.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: Contextual Earnings-22: A Speech Recognition Benchmark with Custom Vocabulary in the Wild
papers.authors: Berkin Durmus, Chen Cen, Eduardo Pacheco, Arda Okan, Atila Orhon
papers.problem: Academic ASR metrics underweight rare custom vocabulary.
papers.method: Realistic vocabulary contexts and keyword prompting/boosting baselines over Earnings-22 clips.
papers.results: The official Hugging Face test split exposes 772 rows; inspected examples are 15-second clips.
papers.relevance: Useful later for controlled technical-term recognition and vocabulary distractors.
papers.limit: Clips and custom-vocabulary lists are not themselves full meeting-history QA or tool-call annotations.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: FinCall-Surprise: A Large Scale Multi-modal Benchmark for Earning Surprise Prediction
papers.authors: Dong Shu, Yanguang Liu, Huopu Zhang, Mengnan Du
papers.problem: Multimodal earnings research lacks accessible paired data.
papers.method: Calls paired with audio, transcripts and presentation slides, evaluated for earnings-surprise prediction.
papers.results: 2,688 calls from 2019–2021; paper evaluates 26 models and warns about label imbalance.
papers.relevance: A promising larger pool after the small ConEC pilot.
papers.limit: GitHub has all text but only small audio/slide samples; full media are external archives. Alignment, speaker IDs, document availability and redistribution were not audited here.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: MAEC: A Multimodal Aligned Earnings Conference Call Dataset for Financial Risk Prediction
papers.authors: Jiazheng Li, Linyi Yang, Barry Smyth, Ruihai Dong
papers.problem: Paired earnings text/audio for financial-risk research is limited.
papers.method: Iterative forced alignment and released transcripts/audio features.
papers.results: Official repository exposes text.txt, features.csv and external MFCC feature archives.
papers.limit: Released features cannot substitute for waveform audio in streaming question injection; no matched slide/release inventory was verified.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: FinQA: A Dataset of Numerical Reasoning over Financial Data
papers.problem: Numerical reasoning over heterogeneous financial reports needs explainable supervision.
papers.method: Expert-written financial-report questions with gold reasoning programs.
papers.results: Provides explicit arithmetic reasoning supervision; popular models lag expert humans.
papers.relevance: Useful templates for grounded calculator calls and numeric answer checking.
papers.limit: Document QA, not timestamped multi-speaker conversation; do not pretend its expert questions were spoken call requests.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

papers.title: TAT-QA: A Question Answering Benchmark on a Hybrid of Tabular and Textual Content in Finance
papers.problem: Financial answers often combine table cells and explanatory prose.
papers.method: Hybrid table/text contexts, expert questions and symbolic aggregation.
papers.results: Official project reports 16,552 questions over 2,757 hybrid contexts.
papers.relevance: Page/table provenance, units and numerical operators for a future document tool.
papers.limit: Not streaming history QA. Expert finance wording is a reference for useful content, not a model for casual spoken phrasing.
papers.verification: primary paper abstract and/or official project repository checked 2026-10-26

themes: Use complete calls for history, short contextual-ASR clips for lexical stress, and document QA for tool supervision; these serve different purposes.
Realistic context contains distracting names and numbers; context extracted from future dialogue must be excluded.
Existing papers motivate the ingredients, but they do not supply natural participant-to-assistant requests with causal cutoffs.

gaps.statement: Natural short participant-to-assistant questions linked to past evidence and current motivation remain to be constructed.
gaps.evidence: ConEC/Earnings datasets evaluate ASR; FinQA/TAT-QA evaluate static documents. This is our inference about the inspected task definitions, not a universal novelty claim.

gaps.statement: Document availability, speaker identity and timing quality need explicit audit before streaming replay.
gaps.evidence: ConEC timestamp README, missing boundaries in both inspected calls, and speaker rosters from third-party full-call sources.

gaps.statement: Tool use needs a source-page and arithmetic audit, including abstention when sources are unavailable.
gaps.evidence: Our two PDF fixtures demonstrate table lookups; an autonomous tool policy has not been tested.

search_angles: contextual ASR earnings calls slides releases
FinCall Surprise full audio slides repository
